attempts.hypothesis: AC-4 is narrower than stated: the workspace picker path (`/devcontainer use` with 2+ matching entries) does not bind the container the operator picked, because `picked.ambiguous` is false for a stopped candidate and `primaryCandidate(picked)?.id` silently takes candidates[0].
attempts.method: Read src/commands.ts:534-546 and considered a workspace with 2 running containers plus a stopped sibling. Built a probe that reproduced the reported behaviour (one prompt answered with the container label, bind candidate undefined, answer '[ambiguous-candidate]'), then instrumented the command layer itself (patched dist/src/commands.js and the type-stripped src/commands.ts) to log which picker each answer reached.
attempts.evidence: The end-to-end behaviour is correct once the picker answers are aligned to the prompt actually shown. Instrumented run against src/commands.ts (real Node process): PROMPT 0 "Select the container for /ws/project-b" -> BOUND {"status":"selected-stopped","candidate":{"id":"zz9","state":"exited"}} -> RESULT "Selected `/ws/project-b` → container `zz9`." Identical result against the emitted dist and against the in-memory module. The author's neighbouring test ('offers the container picker for an ambiguous workspace chosen from the workspace picker') passes and does assert candidateId === 'b2'. The earlier contradictory observation was an artefact of my own probe answering the FIRST prompt with a container label, which the workspace picker consumed (labels.indexOf === -1 -> '[unexpected] Unknown selection.'); the container-picker answer is then also consumed as the workspace answer with index 0, producing '[ambiguous-candidate]'. `git diff --exit-code -- dist` is clean, so dist is not stale. No user-visible defect. outcome_note: Also probed the guard-vs-fixture mismatch: the workspace-picker labels are built from the registry entry label (e.g. 'zz9 — exited — devcontainer:latest') but the branch answers '[ambiguous-candidate]' whenever the container labels contain 2+ running entries — the two lists carry different vocabularies textually (registration name vs Docker image), but passing the list index instead of the label string would remove the one way to consume the wrong answer. Not a defect in the claim; noted as a robustness nit only.

attempts.hypothesis: AC-4 depends on registry fields that the picker is given but that discovery may not populate (id / state / image), so the picker would mis-answer for the ambiguous case.
attempts.method: Read src/runtime/host-discovery.ts:340-373 (candidates carry id, mapped state, and image only when `c.image` is non-empty) and src/commands.ts chooseAmbiguousContainer label construction; then ran the real discovery mapping path against an entry without an image.
attempts.evidence: The label drops the image segment when absent (`c.image !== undefined ? ... : ""`), and selection resolution uses the label LIST INDEX, not the parsed label text — so a missing image cannot corrupt the choice. Missing `id` cannot reach the picker: discovery filters `c.id !== ""` before building containerCandidates. outcome_note:

attempts.method: Traced every `mappingFor`/`readMapping` call site (execution-service.ts:185-214 for `container-exec`, extensions/index.ts:285-311 for both guards) and read the service-level test that exercises the guard through the real ExecutionService (tests/unit/service-routing-guard.test.ts).

attempts.hypothesis: AC-3 is narrower or wider than stated: the guard could fire on a substring of an unrelated flag or value, or miss a legitimate host path, or be defeated by a form the tests do not cover.
attempts.method: Drove `detectHostPathOnContainerSurface` (from the emitted dist) over 18 argv shapes and 6 mapping variants: exact host path, beneath it, prefix-sharing sibling, relative text, `--prefix=<host>`, `P=<host>`, shell text inside an element, trailing slash, trailing `//x`, leading `//`, `.`-normalised, `-v host:/src`, root host path, empty host path, ancestor/nested container paths, same-path mapping, and no mapping.
attempts.evidence: Fires exactly on elements that ARE the host path or lie beneath it with a real `/` boundary, and never on the relative/flag/quote-disfigured forms (`//data/work/proj`, `/data/work/./proj/x`, `-v host:/src` all return undefined — conservative false negatives, documented as 'a false negative costs nothing beyond the status quo'). The exemptions behave as the comments claim: same-path mount is exempt (and `samePathMounts` correctly refuses a target-only shadow and correctly expands `${localWorkspaceFolder}`), the nested container workspace is exempt while a host sibling under the same host path is refused, and the ancestor case refuses everything under the host path. outcome_note:

attempts.hypothesis: AC-1 duplicates or contradicts the audit trail, or leaks a credential the audit trail redacts, or its accounting is wrong.
attempts.method: Read src/host-run-ledger.ts, src/host-runner.ts (`note()` on denial, guard violation, spawn failure and success) and extensions/index.ts:536-577 (ledger reset + `setCapture` on session_start; the withheld-attempt path on `devcontainer_host_exec`). Executed redactText/commandIdentity/the ledger directly with bearer-token, `--password=`, URL-credential, `API_KEY=` and `-u user:pass` argv; also exercised capture-mode switching.
attempts.evidence: Every record-shaped field in the ledger is redacted with the same `redactText` the audit path uses ('curl -H authorization: Bearer sk-live-abcdef123456' -> 'curl -H authorization: [REDACTED] [REDACTED]'); `commandCapture: "none"` both withholds text and CLEARS already-retained text, so the summary cannot become the one place a policy-declined command is readable, while the count still reflects attempts; `fingerprint-only` (the default) emits no `commandText` so the operator summary never contains text a non-operator-facing mode would have withheld. The ledger is bounded (limit 5), resets per session, and reports the first attempt once (including a refused or guard-denied one). A reminder: the ledger adds no timestamp/output/identity, so it is genuinely a summary and not a second record — consistent with the claim's own wording. outcome_note: Two observations that are NOT defects but are worth the author knowing: (a) redactText does not cover the `-u user:pass` idiom or a bare assignment without a secret-looking key name ("P=/path") — both are also uncovered in the audit trail when `commandCapture: "redacted-text"`, so the ledger is not weaker than the declared record, but the CHANGELOG sentence 'redacted with the same rules the audit trail uses, so a credential cannot reach the status text' reads stronger than the rules support; (b) renderStatus() takes the workspace from the selected snapshot while sharing the same `host runs` line, which deliberately mixes host-run visibility into container-target rendering — matches REQ-1's wording, so no finding.
